newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS AFTER FIRST GIANT SLALOM RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI LEADS AFTER FIRST GIANT SLALOM RUN.

text.p: Italy's world champion Deborah Compagnoni tamed a bumpy course to lead the fourth women's World Cup giant slalom of the season after the first run on Friday.
Compagnoni showed good rhythm and control through a tight set of gates to clock one minute 3.69 seconds, 1.08 seconds ahead of Germany's Katja Seizinger, the joint World Cup leader in the discipline.
Austrian Anita Wachter, the winner on the Zwiesel course the last time the World Cup came here in 1991, was lying third with 1:05.03, according to provisional results.
The second run was due to start at 1230 GMT.

Sweden's overall World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg, who has struggled with her form in giant slalom recently, boosted her confidence with the sixth fastest time of 1:05.81, 2.12 seconds behind Compagnoni.
Italy's Sabina Panzanini, who has won two of the three giant slaloms so far this season, looked uncomfortable on the course, which was icy in parts, and finished outside the top 15.
